subject: maths
title: Factors and Multiples
seo_title: Year 5 Factors and Multiples Worksheets: Factor Pairs, Factor Trees and Divisibility Rules
standard_text: Express natural numbers as products of their factors, recognise multiples and determine if one number is divisible by another
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on factors and multiples: factor pairs, writing numbers as products of factors, factor trees, multiples and divisibility rules for 2, 3, 5, 9 and 10. 100 questions with an answer key, aligned to the Australian Curriculum and useful for NAPLAN practice.
key_big: A factor divides a number exactly; a multiple is in its times table.
key_sub: 4 is a factor of 12, and 12 is a multiple of 4. 1 and the number itself are always factors. To test 3 or 9, add the digits.
body_html:
Factors and factor pairs

A factor divides a number exactly, with no remainder. Factors come in pairs that multiply to make the number. 3 × 4 = 12, so 3 and 4 are a factor pair of 12.

To find all the factors, test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order. Stop when the pairs meet. 1 and the number itself are always factors.

Example

Find all the factors of 30.

1 × 30, 2 × 15, 3 × 10, 5 × 6. 4 does not divide 30. The next number, 6, is already in a pair, so stop.

Answer: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30

Writing a number as a product of factors

A product is the answer to a multiplication. One number can be written as a product in many ways: 24 = 3 × 8 = 4 × 6 = 2 × 3 × 4. A factor tree keeps splitting a number into factor pairs.

The circled numbers 2 and 3 cannot be split any further: they are prime numbers, with exactly two factors. You will meet primes in Year 6.

Example

Write 40 as a product of three factors.

40 = 8 × 5, and 8 = 2 × 4.

Answer: 40 = 2 × 4 × 5

Multiples

A multiple is in a number’s times table: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35 … are multiples of 7. 4 is a factor of 12, and 12 is a multiple of 4.

Example

Is 54 a multiple of 6?

Count in 6s or use a fact: 6 × 9 = 54.

Answer: Yes

Divisibility rules

“Divisible by 3” means 3 divides the number with no remainder. These quick checks save time:

Divisible byCheckExample
2The last digit is even (0, 2, 4, 6, 8)538
5The last digit is 0 or 5735
10The last digit is 04990
3The digits add to a multiple of 3471: 4 + 7 + 1 = 12
9The digits add to a multiple of 9738: 7 + 3 + 8 = 18

For any other number, divide and look at the remainder: 96 ÷ 8 = 12, so 96 is divisible by 8.

Example

Is 1236 divisible by 3? Is it divisible by 9?

1 + 2 + 3 + 6 = 12. 12 is a multiple of 3 but not of 9.

Answer: Divisible by 3, not by 9

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up factors and multiples: 4 is a multiple of 124 is a factor of 12; 12 is a multiple of 4
Missing a factor pairTest 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order until the pairs meet
Forgetting 1 and the number itselfEvery number has 1 and itself as factors
Using the digit sum to test 4, 6 or 8The digit sum works only for 3 and 9. Divide to check 4
Looking at the first digit to test 2, 5 or 10Look at the last digit
Thinking 27 is a multiple of 7 because it has a 727 ÷ 7 = 3 r 6. Digits do not decide

faq.q: What is the difference between a factor and a multiple?
faq.a: A factor divides a number exactly, and a multiple is in its times table. 4 is a factor of 12, and 12 is a multiple of 4.

faq.q: What do Year 5 students learn about factors and multiples in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: In Year 5 (AC9M5N02) students write numbers as products of their factors, recognise multiples and work out whether one number is divisible by another. Prime and composite numbers follow in Year 6.

faq.q: What are the divisibility rules for 3 and 9?
faq.a: Add the digits. If the sum is a multiple of 3, the number is divisible by 3; if it is a multiple of 9, the number is divisible by 9. For 471, 4 + 7 + 1 = 12, so it is divisible by 3 but not 9.

faq.q: Is 1 a factor of every number?
faq.a: Yes. 1 divides every whole number exactly, and every number is also a factor of itself. So 1 and the number are always a factor pair.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 12?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Do not forget 1 and 12, and do not miss 3 × 4. 12, 24, 36, 48 are multiples of 12, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 20?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 20, 2 × 10, 4 × 5. So the factors are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Do not forget 1 and 20, and do not miss 4 × 5. 20, 40, 60, 80 are multiples of 20, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 18?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 18, 2 × 9, 3 × 6. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Do not forget 1 and 18, and do not miss 3 × 6. 18, 36, 54, 72 are multiples of 18, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 30?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 30, 2 × 15, 3 × 10, 5 × 6. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. Do not forget 1 and 30, and do not miss 5 × 6. 30, 60, 90, 120 are multiples of 30, not factors.

items.q: This array shows 18 dots. Which factor pair of 18 does it show?
items.e: There are 3 rows of 6 dots: 3 × 6 = 18. So 3 × 6 is a factor pair of 18. 2 × 9 is another pair, but it is not the one shown, and 3 + 6 = 9, not 18.
There are 4 rows of 7 dots: 4 × 7 = 28. So 4 × 7 is a factor pair of 28. 2 × 14 is another pair, but it is not the one shown, and 4 + 7 = 11, not 28.

items.q: Which of these is a factor pair of 36?
items.e: 4 × 9 = 36, so 4 and 9 are a factor pair. 6 × 5 = 30, 3 × 13 = 39 and 2 × 16 = 32. The other pairs of 36 are 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12 and 6 × 6.

items.q: The factor rainbow shows all the factors of 24. Which number is missing?
items.e: The arc joins ? to 3, so 3 × ? = 24. 24 ÷ 3 = 8. 21 is 24 − 3, not 24 ÷ 3. 9 and 7 are not factors of 24.

items.q: The factor rainbow shows all the factors of 30. Which number is missing?
items.e: The arc joins ? to 2, so 2 × ? = 30. 30 ÷ 2 = 15. 28 is 30 − 2, 60 is 30 × 2, and 10 is already in the rainbow (it pairs with 3).

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 32?
items.e: 32 ÷ 6 = 5 remainder 2, so 6 is not a factor of 32. 4 × 8 = 32. 8 × 4 = 32. 16 × 2 = 32.

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 45?
items.e: 45 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 3, so 6 is not a factor of 45. 3 × 15 = 45. 9 × 5 = 45. 15 × 3 = 45.

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 56?
Which number is a factor of 42?
items.e: 7 × 6 = 42, so 7 is a factor of 42. 84 is a multiple of 42, not a factor, and 8 and 12 leave a remainder.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 54?
items.e: 9 × 6 = 54, so 9 is a factor of 54. 108 is a multiple of 54, not a factor, and 8 and 12 leave a remainder.

items.q: How many factors does 16 have?
items.e: The factor pairs are 1 × 16, 2 × 8 and 4 × 4. The factors are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16: 5 factors. 4 × 4 uses 4 only once, so do not count it twice (6). 3 is the number of pairs.

items.q: Ethan lists the factor pairs of 48: 1 × 48, 2 × 24, 3 × 16, 6 × 8. Which pair did he miss?
items.e: Test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order. 48 ÷ 4 = 12, so 4 × 12 is missing. 8 × 6 is the same pair as 6 × 8. 5 × 10 = 50 and 7 × 7 = 49, not 48.

items.q: Mia says the factors of 15 are 3 and 5. Which factors has she left out?
c: None. That is all of them
items.e: 1 × 15 = 15 is a factor pair too. The factors of 15 are 1, 3, 5 and 15, so she left out 1 and 15. 1 is a factor of every number, and every number is a factor of itself. 30 and 45 are multiples of 15.

items.q: Charlotte says 7 is a factor of 27 because 27 has a 7 in it. Is she right?
items.e: 7 × 3 = 21 and 7 × 4 = 28, so 27 is not in the 7 times table. 27 ÷ 7 = 3 remainder 6, so 7 is not a factor. The digits of a number do not tell you its factors.

items.q: What is the largest factor of 35 that is less than 35?
items.e: The factors of 35 are 1, 5, 7 and 35. The largest one below 35 is 7. 34 is 35 − 1, and 35 ÷ 2 is not a whole number, so 17 is not a factor.

items.q: How many factors does 24 have?
items.e: The factor pairs are 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8 and 4 × 6. Each pair gives 2 factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. That is 8 factors. 4 is the number of pairs, 6 leaves out 1 and 24, and 48 is a multiple of 24.

sets.title: Writing a number as a product of factors

items.q: Which shows 24 as a product of two factors?
items.e: A product is the answer to a multiplication. 3 × 8 = 24, so 3 × 8 shows 24 as a product of two factors. 20 + 4 adds, so it is a sum, not a product; 2 × 14 = 28; 4 × 5 = 20.

items.q: Which shows 36 as a product of two factors?
items.e: A product is the answer to a multiplication. 4 × 9 = 36, so 4 × 9 shows 36 as a product of two factors. 30 + 6 adds, so it is a sum, not a product; 6 × 7 = 42; 4 × 8 = 32.

items.q: Which shows 24 as a product of three factors?
items.e: 2 × 3 = 6 and 6 × 4 = 24. 2 × 3 × 5 = 30, 2 × 12 has only two factors, and 2 + 10 + 12 is a sum.

items.q: Find the missing factor: 30 = 2 × 3 × ?
items.e: Multiply the factors you know: 2 × 3 = 6. Then 30 ÷ 6 = 5. Check: 2 × 3 × 5 = 30. 15 is 30 ÷ 2 and 10 is 30 ÷ 3: each uses only one of the factors. 25 is 30 − 2 − 3.

items.q: Find the missing factor: 40 = 2 × ? × 5
items.e: Multiply the factors you know: 2 × 5 = 10. Then 40 ÷ 10 = 4. Check: 2 × 4 × 5 = 40. 20 is 40 ÷ 2 and 8 is 40 ÷ 5: each uses only one of the factors. 33 is 40 − 2 − 5.

items.q: Find the missing factor: 48 = 4 × ?
Which number sentence does this factor tree show?
items.e: Multiply the circled numbers at the ends of the branches: 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 24. 2 × 2 × 3 = 12 misses one 2. 4 and 6 have already been split, so do not use them again. 2 + 2 + 2 + 3 = 9 adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: Which number sentence does this factor tree show?
items.e: Multiply the circled numbers: 2 × 2 = 4, 3 × 3 = 9, 4 × 9 = 36. 2 × 3 = 6 counts each number only once. 4 and 9 have already been split. 2 + 2 + 3 + 3 = 10 adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: What number is missing from this factor tree?
items.e: 40 splits into a factor pair: 8 × ? = 40. 40 ÷ 8 = 5. 32 is 40 − 8. 4 and 10 are factors of 40, but 8 × 4 = 32 and 8 × 10 = 80.

items.q: What is 2 × 2 × 3 × 5?
items.e: 2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 3 = 12, 12 × 5 = 60. 12 comes from adding (2 + 2 + 3 + 5), 30 uses only one 2, and 120 uses three 2s.

items.q: Which is not equal to 36?
items.e: 5 × 7 = 35, not 36. 2 × 18, 3 × 12 and 6 × 6 all equal 36: they are factor pairs of 36.

items.q: Which is equal to 2 × 3 × 4?
items.e: 2 × 3 = 6, so 2 × 3 × 4 = 6 × 4 = 24. 5 × 4 adds 2 + 3, 2 × 7 adds 3 + 4, and 9 adds all three.

items.q: Work out 4 × 7 × 5. Tip: multiply 4 × 5 first.
items.e: You can multiply in any order. 4 × 5 = 20, then 20 × 7 = 140. 16 is 4 + 7 + 5, 28 forgets the × 5, and 280 is 4 × 7 × 10.

items.q: Work out 2 × 9 × 5.
items.e: 2 × 5 = 10, then 10 × 9 = 90. 16 is 2 + 9 + 5, 18 forgets the × 5, and 45 forgets the × 2.

items.q: In how many ways can you write 12 as a product of two whole numbers? (3 × 4 and 4 × 3 count as one way.)
items.e: 1 × 12, 2 × 6 and 3 × 4: 3 ways. 6 is the number of factors, not pairs. 2 forgets 1 × 12, and 4 counts one pair twice.

items.q: Write 8 as a product of three factors, each greater than 1.
items.e: 8 = 2 × 4 and 4 = 2 × 2, so 8 = 2 × 2 × 2. 2 × 4 has only two factors, 1 × 2 × 4 uses 1, and 2 × 2 × 4 = 16.

items.q: Which number is equal to 3 × 4 × 5?
items.e: 3 × 4 = 12, then 12 × 5 = 60. 12 is 3 + 4 + 5, 20 is only 4 × 5, and 345 writes the digits side by side.

items.q: Which is not a way to write 18 as a product of factors?
100 = 4 × 25. Find the missing factor: 100 = 2 × 2 × 5 × ?
72 = 8 × 9. Find the missing factor: 72 = 8 × 3 × ?
Which number is a multiple of 6?
items.e: 6 × 7 = 42, so 42 is a multiple of 6. 16 ÷ 6 = 2 remainder 4. 26 ÷ 6 = 4 remainder 2. 63 ÷ 6 = 10 remainder 3. Having a 6 as a digit does not make a number a multiple of 6.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 8?
items.e: 8 × 9 = 72, so 72 is a multiple of 8. 28 ÷ 8 = 3 remainder 4. 18 ÷ 8 = 2 remainder 2. 84 ÷ 8 = 10 remainder 4. Having an 8 as a digit does not make a number a multiple of 8.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 9?
items.e: 9 × 9 = 81, so 81 is a multiple of 9. 19 ÷ 9 = 2 remainder 1. 39 ÷ 9 = 4 remainder 3. 89 ÷ 9 = 9 remainder 8. Having a 9 as a digit does not make a number a multiple of 9.

items.q: Which number is not a multiple of 7?
items.e: 7 × 6 = 42 and 7 × 7 = 49, so 47 is not in the 7 times table. 7 × 7 = 49, 7 × 8 = 56 and 7 × 5 = 35.

items.q: What is the 6th multiple of 8?
items.e: The 6th multiple of 8 is 8 × 6 = 48. 40 is the 5th multiple, 56 is the 7th, and 14 is 8 + 6.

items.q: Which list shows the first five multiples of 7?
items.e: The multiples of 7 are 7 × 1, 7 × 2, 7 × 3 …: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35. The first multiple is 7 itself. 1, 7 are the factors of 7, and 7, 17, 27 … add 10 each time.

items.q: Zara shades the multiples of 3 on this number track. Which multiple of 3 has she missed?
items.e: Count in 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. 3 × 5 = 15 is not shaded. 13 has a 3 as a digit, but 13 ÷ 3 = 4 remainder 1. 16 and 10 are not multiples of 3.

items.q: Is 54 a multiple of 6?
items.e: 6 × 9 = 54, so yes, 54 is a multiple of 6. Multiples of 6 do not have to end in 6 (12, 18, 24 …). 6 × 8 = 48, so 54 ÷ 6 is not 8 r 6: a remainder of 6 means one more 6 fits.

items.q: Cooper says 30 is a factor of 5. Is he right?
items.e: 5 × 6 = 30, so 30 is a multiple of 5, and 5 is a factor of 30. A factor divides the number; a multiple is in its times table.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: 7 × 8 = 56, so 7 is a factor of 56 (and 56 is a multiple of 7). 56 ÷ 6 = 9 remainder 2, so 6 is not a factor of 56.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of both 4 and 6?
items.e: 4 × 3 = 12 and 6 × 2 = 12, so 12 is a multiple of both. 10 is 4 + 6. 18 is a multiple of 6 only, and 16 is a multiple of 4 only.

items.q: What is the next multiple of 9 after 63?
items.e: 63 = 9 × 7, so the next multiple is 9 × 8 = 72. 64 adds 1, 73 adds 10, and 81 = 9 × 9 skips 72.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 25?
items.e: Multiples of 25 end in 00, 25, 50 or 75. 25 × 7 = 175. 155 and 205 end in 5, so they are multiples of 5, but not of 25. 260 ends in 60.

items.q: How many multiples of 6 are there from 1 to 50?
items.e: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48: 8 multiples. 6 × 9 = 54 is more than 50, so 9 is too many. 7 means one was missed, and 10 counts in 5s.

items.q: Leo counts in 4s from 4. Which number will he say?
items.e: 4 × 16 = 64, so 64 is in the count. 42, 54 and 70 are even, but each leaves a remainder of 2 when divided by 4. Even numbers are not all multiples of 4.

items.q: Which list shows only multiples of 5?
items.e: Multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5. 15, 40, 65, 90 all do. 51 and 52 have a 5 in them but end in 1 and 2. 1 and 5 are the factors of 5.

items.q: What is the 100th multiple of 7?
Mei says 12 is a multiple of 24. Is she right?
c: Yes. 12 is in the 24 times table
items.e: 12 × 2 = 24, so 24 is a multiple of 12, and 12 is a factor of 24. A multiple of 24 is 24 or more: 24, 48, 72 …

items.q: Which multiple of 8 is closest to 50?
items.e: 8 × 6 = 48 and 8 × 7 = 56. 48 is 2 away from 50, and 56 is 6 away, so the answer is 48. 40 is 10 away, and 50 is not a multiple of 8 (50 ÷ 8 = 6 r 2).

items.q: I am a multiple of 7 between 40 and 50. I am an odd number. What number am I?
items.e: The multiples of 7 between 40 and 50 are 42 and 49. 42 is even, so the answer is 49 (7 × 7). 47 and 45 are odd but not multiples of 7.

items.q: Which number is divisible by 2?
items.e: A number is divisible by 2 if its last digit is even (0, 2, 4, 6 or 8). 538 ends in 8. 825 starts with an even digit and 467 has even digits in it, but they end in 5 and 7. 2001 ends in 1.

items.q: Which number is divisible by 5?
items.e: A number is divisible by 5 if it ends in 0 or 5. 735 ends in 5. 557, 5052 and 508 have 5s in them, but they end in 7, 2 and 8.

items.q: Which number is divisible by 10?
items.e: A number is divisible by 10 if it ends in 0. 4990 ends in 0. 1005 ends in 5 (it is divisible by 5, not 10). 1001 and 4099 end in 1 and 9.

items.q: Which number is divisible by 3?
items.e: Add the digits. If the sum is a multiple of 3, the number is divisible by 3. 4 + 7 + 1 = 12, so 471 works (471 = 3 × 157). 473 ends in 3 but 4 + 7 + 3 = 14. 3401 starts with 3 but 3 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 8. 5 + 3 + 2 = 10.

items.q: Which number is divisible by 9?
items.e: Add the digits. If the sum is a multiple of 9, the number is divisible by 9. 7 + 3 + 8 = 18, so 738 works (738 = 9 × 82). 919 and 829 have digit sums of 19, and 9001 has 10. Having a 9 in the number does not matter.

items.q: Which number is divisible by 3 but not by 9?
items.e: 5 + 7 = 12. 12 is a multiple of 3 but not of 9, so 57 (= 3 × 19) is divisible by 3 only. 8 + 1 = 9, so 81 is divisible by both. 5 + 8 = 13 and 4 + 4 = 8, so 58 and 44 are not divisible by 3.

items.q: Jack says 316 is not divisible by 4, because 3 + 1 + 6 = 10 and 10 is not a multiple of 4. Is he right?
c: Yes. 10 is not a multiple of 4
items.e: The digit-sum rule only works for 3 and 9. It does not work for 4. 4 × 79 = 316, so 316 is divisible by 4. 316 is even, and 10 is not a multiple of 4.

items.q: Which digit can go in the box to make 47□ divisible by 3?
items.e: 4 + 7 = 11. The digit sum must be a multiple of 3: 11 + 1 = 12 works, so 1 (471). 4 or 7 would also work. 3 gives 14, 0 gives 11 and 2 gives 13. The last digit being 3 does not help.

items.q: Which digit can go in the box to make 5□4 divisible by 9?
items.e: 5 + 4 = 9. The digit sum must be a multiple of 9: 9 + 9 = 18 works, so 9 (594 = 9 × 66). 6 gives 564: 5 + 6 + 4 = 15, which is a multiple of 3 but not of 9. 3 gives 12 and 1 gives 10.

items.q: Which number is divisible by both 2 and 5?
items.e: Divisible by 2 means the last digit is even. Divisible by 5 means it ends in 0 or 5. Both together means it ends in 0: 370. 255 and 525 are odd, and 252 does not end in 0 or 5.

items.q: Which number is divisible by 2, 3 and 5?
items.e: It must end in 0 (for 2 and 5) and have a digit sum that is a multiple of 3. 2 + 4 + 0 = 6, so 240 works. 250 has digit sum 7, 245 is odd, and 236 does not end in 0 or 5.

items.q: Is 96 divisible by 8?
items.e: 8 × 10 = 80 and 8 × 2 = 16, so 8 × 12 = 96. Yes, 96 is divisible by 8. The digit sum only works for 3 and 9. A remainder of 8 means one more 8 fits, and 8 × 11 = 88.

items.q: Which number divides 91 exactly?
items.e: 7 × 13 = 91, so 7 divides 91 exactly. 9 + 1 = 10, which is not a multiple of 3 or 9. 91 is odd, so 2 does not divide it.

items.q: Which number divides 135 exactly?
items.e: 1 + 3 + 5 = 9, so 135 is divisible by 9: 135 = 9 × 15. 135 is odd, so 2 and 4 do not divide it, and it does not end in 0, so 10 does not divide it.

items.q: Is 132 divisible by 6?
c: No. It does not end in 6
items.e: 6 × 22 = 132, so yes. A quick check: 132 is even (divisible by 2) and 1 + 3 + 2 = 6 (divisible by 3), so it is divisible by 6. Multiples of 6 do not have to end in 6. 6 × 21 = 126, and 132 − 126 = 6, so 21 r 2 is wrong.

items.q: Which number is not divisible by 3?
items.e: 1 + 0 + 4 + 5 = 10, which is not a multiple of 3, so 1045 is not divisible by 3. 1035 has digit sum 9, 2001 has 3, and 1236 has 12: all multiples of 3.

items.q: Which number is divisible by 9?
items.e: 3 + 7 + 2 + 6 = 18, so 3726 is divisible by 9 (3726 = 9 × 414). 3729 has digit sum 21: divisible by 3 but not 9. 9100 has 10 and 1999 has 28.

items.q: Which numbers is 450 divisible by?
items.e: 450 ends in 0, so it is divisible by 2, 5 and 10. 4 + 5 + 0 = 9, so it is divisible by 3 and 9. The answer is 2, 3, 5, 9 and 10.

items.q: If a number is divisible by 9, which number must it also be divisible by?
items.e: 9 = 3 × 3, so every multiple of 9 is also a multiple of 3. 9 itself is not divisible by 18, 6 or 2, so those do not always work.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: 5 + 4 = 9, and 9 × 6 = 54, so 54 is divisible by 9. 9 ÷ 54 is not a whole number. 54 ÷ 4 = 13 r 2, and 54 does not end in 0 or 5.

sets.title: Word problems with factors and multiples

items.q: A teacher puts 36 chairs in equal rows for a class assembly, with none left over. Which could not be the number of chairs in each row?
items.e: The number in each row must be a factor of 36. 36 ÷ 8 = 4 remainder 4, so 8 chairs does not work. 4 × 9 = 36 and 6 × 6 = 36.

items.q: A school hall has 30 chairs. Which layout uses all 30 chairs in equal rows?
24 students make equal teams for sport, with no one left out. Which team size works?
items.e: The team size must be a factor of 24. 24 ÷ 6 = 4, so teams of 6 students give 4 teams. 24 ÷ 5, 24 ÷ 7 and 24 ÷ 9 all leave a remainder.

items.q: Cupcakes for the school fete are packed in boxes of 6. Which number of cupcakes fills the boxes with none left over?
items.e: The number must be a multiple of 6. 6 × 9 = 54. 46, 56 and 64 have a 6 as a digit, but they are not multiples of 6: each leaves a remainder of 4.

items.q: Sausages come in packets of 8. Liam needs at least 30 sausages for the sausage sizzle. What is the fewest packets he can buy?
items.e: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32. 3 packets give 24, which is not enough. 4 packets give 32. 5 packets give 40, which is more than needed.

items.q: 130 students go on a school excursion. Each bus holds 48 students. What is the fewest buses they need?
items.e: Multiples of 48: 48, 96, 144. 2 buses hold 96, which is not enough. 3 buses hold 144. 82 is 130 − 48.

items.q: Amelia has 12 red beads and 18 blue beads. She makes bracelets that are all the same, using every bead. How many bracelets could she make?
items.e: The number of bracelets must be a factor of both 12 and 18. 6 works: each bracelet has 2 red and 3 blue beads, so 6 bracelets. 4 divides 12 but not 18, 9 divides 18 but not 12, and 36 is a multiple, not a factor.

items.q: A class has fewer than 40 students. They can line up in 2s, 3s or 5s with no one left over. How many students are in the class?
items.e: The number must be a multiple of 2, 3 and 5. 2 × 3 × 5 = 30. 10 is not a multiple of 3, and 15 and 35 are odd, so they are not multiples of 2.

items.q: Sienna is between 10 and 15 years old. Her age is a factor of 36 and a multiple of 4. How old is she?
items.e: Factors of 36 between 10 and 15: only 12. 12 = 4 × 3, so it is also a multiple of 4. Sienna is 12. 9 is a factor of 36 but not a multiple of 4, 16 is a multiple of 4 but not a factor of 36, and 14 is neither.

items.q: A square courtyard is paved with 49 square tiles. How many tiles are along each side?
items.e: A square has the same number of tiles along each side, so find a factor pair with two equal numbers: 7 × 7 = 49. There are 7 tiles. 14 is 7 × 2, 49 is the total number of tiles, and 9 × 9 = 81.

items.q: A netball team has 7 players. 63 students want to play. How many full teams can they make?
items.e: 7 × 9 = 63, so they can make 9 teams with no one left over. 7 × 8 = 56 is too few. 56 is 63 − 7, and 70 is 63 + 7.

items.q: Tennis balls come in cans of 4. Which number of balls can you not buy in full cans?
items.e: You can only buy a multiple of 4. 30 ÷ 4 = 7 remainder 2, so 30 balls is not possible. 4 × 6 = 24, 4 × 8 = 32 and 4 × 9 = 36.

items.q: Ruby thinks of a number between 10 and 30. It is a multiple of 4 and a factor of 40. What is her number?
items.e: Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. Between 10 and 30 there is only 20, and 20 = 4 × 5, so the number is 20. 12 and 24 are multiples of 4 but not factors of 40, and 10 is not a multiple of 4.

items.q: 28 students split into equal groups. Each group has more than 1 and fewer than 10 students. How many different group sizes are possible?
items.e: The group size must be a factor of 28: 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28. Between 1 and 10 that leaves 2, 4 and 7: 3 sizes. 6 counts every factor, 4 wrongly includes 14, and 2 misses one.

items.q: At the swimming carnival, 48 students swim in races. Each race fills all 8 lanes. How many races are there?
items.e: 8 × 6 = 48, so there are 6 races. 40 is 48 − 8, 56 is 48 + 8, and 8 × 5 = 40 is too few.

items.q: Chloe has 135 stickers to share equally among 9 friends. Can she do it with none left over?
items.e: 1 + 3 + 5 = 9, so 135 is divisible by 9. 9 × 15 = 135, so yes, 15 each. Odd numbers can still be divisible by 9, and 9 × 14 = 126.

items.q: A farmer packs 100 eggs into cartons of 12. How many cartons can be filled?
items.e: Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96, 108. 96 = 12 × 8, so 8 cartons are full and 4 eggs are left over. 9 cartons need 108 eggs, 4 is the number left over, and 88 is 100 − 12.

items.q: At the zoo, a koala is weighed every 3 days and has a health check every 4 days. Today it has both. In how many days will it next have both on the same day?
items.e: Multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12. Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12. The first number in both lists is 12. 7 is 3 + 4, 24 is also in both lists but it is not the first, and 4 is not a multiple of 3.

items.q: Aarav buys 5 packs of juice boxes. Each pack has 6 boxes. He shares them equally among 10 friends. How many does each friend get?
items.e: 5 × 6 = 30 juice boxes. 30 ÷ 10 = 3 each. 6 is the number in one pack, 2 is 10 ÷ 5, and 20 is 30 − 10.

items.q: I am a multiple of 9 between 100 and 120. I am an even number. What number am I?
items.e: Multiples of 9 between 100 and 120: 108 (1 + 0 + 8 = 9) and 117 (1 + 1 + 7 = 9). 117 is odd, so the answer is 108. 112 has digit sum 4, so it is not a multiple of 9, and 99 is less than 100.
